query: Upcoming U.S.-Argentina diplomatic events, summits, or high-level visits between August 19 and September 10, 2026 that could host a nuclear cooperation agreement signing
answer:
Research complete. Key findings:

**The window is empty of hosting opportunities.** No bilateral summit, ministerial, or announced signing ceremony falls between 19 Aug and 10 Sept 2026. Milei's next foreign travel begins 22 September (UNGA); before that he has only domestic events (Council of the Americas 20 Aug, Rosario 21 Aug).

**The IAEA General Conference narrowly misses:** 14–18 September 2026, Vienna — 4 to 8 days after the window closes. This is the most natural multilateral venue for a nuclear signing and it sits just outside.

**The agreement itself is genuinely advanced but targeted later.** A replacement 123 Agreement is pending (current one expires 16 Oct 2027). The 19th JSCNEC (Washington, 25–27 Feb 2026) committed to "swiftly complete negotiations"; by 10 Aug 2026 Casa Rosada was saying the text is closed between technical teams with only diplomatic coordination remaining — but the stated target is **before end of 2026**, not this window. No 20th JSCNEC has been scheduled.

**Two findings that cut against a purely calendar-based read:**
1. The Paraguay precedent (4 Aug 2026) shows Rubio signing a civil nuclear MOU with a visiting foreign minister at the State Department on an ordinary working day — no summit required. Quirno travels to Washington frequently and on short notice.
2. There *is* senior U.S. presence in Buenos Aires inside the window — DEA Administrator Terrence Cole and State's Cartwright Weiland (17–22 Aug) for the 40th IDEC conference — but it is entirely law-enforcement, with no nuclear component.

**Two caveats worth carrying forward:** the "text is closed" claim traces to a single originating source (TN, 10 Aug) syndicated across many outlets, and is stronger than the official joint-statement language. And signing ≠ entry into force — a 123 Agreement then needs 90 days of continuous congressional session.

No prediction markets exist on this question across Polymarket, Manifold, or Kalshi.

One tooling note: AskNews returned 403s (tier-restricted to deepseek-basic / Spelunker+), so all research went through Exa, web search, and direct fetches. The IAEA's own GC70 page also blocks fetching (403), so those dates are corroborated via SNETP, the IAEA's 2026 events preview, and several independent listings rather than the primary page.

key_facts: NO bilateral summit, ministerial, or announced signing ceremony is scheduled between the U.S. and Argentina in the 19 Aug - 10 Sept 2026 window.

Milei has no U.S. trip in the window. His confirmed upcoming U.S./foreign travel: UNGA 81 New York (departs 22 Sept, general debate 22/23-28 Sept), Paris Argentina Week (29 Sept - 2 Oct), Washington Official Hispanic Heritage Gala (13-14 Oct, his 19th U.S. trip), G20 Miami (14-15 Dec). No new Milei-Trump bilateral confirmed for any of them.

The 70th IAEA General Conference is 14-18 September 2026 in Vienna - 4 to 8 days AFTER the window closes. It is the most natural multilateral venue for a nuclear signing and it falls outside the window.

What is pending is a new Section 123 Agreement (Agreement for Cooperation Concerning the Peaceful Uses of Nuclear Energy) to replace the current one. Current agreement: signed Buenos Aires 29 Feb 1996, entered into force 16 Oct 1997, 30-year term, expires 16 October 2027.

19th JSCNEC (Joint Standing Committee on Nuclear Energy Cooperation) met in Washington DC 25-27 Feb 2026; joint statement said both sides 'reaffirmed their commitment to swiftly complete negotiations on the text of a new Agreement.' Co-chaired by Gonzalo Suarez (U.S. DAS for Nonproliferation Policy) and Federico Ramos Napoli (Argentine Secretary of Nuclear Affairs).

On 10 Aug 2026, Argentine press (TN, Ignacio Salerno, widely syndicated) reported Casa Rosada saying the treaty text is CLOSED between technical teams and Cancilleria is coordinating with Washington on diplomatic steps to sign 'during the coming months' - with a stated target of before end of 2026, not within the Aug 19-Sept 10 window.
No 20th JSCNEC meeting has been announced.
After signature, a 123 Agreement requires 90 days of continuous session congressional review in the U.S. before entry into force. Signing does not equal entry into force.

Key precedent: on 4 August 2026 Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed a Memorandum of Understanding for Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation (NCMOU) with Paraguayan FM Ruben Ramirez Lezcano at the Department of State - a low-key working-day ceremony requiring no summit. Casa Rosada explicitly noted an NCMOU is NOT a 123 Agreement.

High-level U.S. presence in Buenos Aires DOES occur inside the window, but is law-enforcement focused: the 40th International Drug Enforcement Conference (IDEC), 18-20 Aug 2026, opened by DEA Administrator Terrence Cole and Argentine Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva. Closed to press, 400-1000 delegates. No nuclear component.
State Department Assistant Secretary for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs Cartwright Weiland was on travel to Argentina 17-22 August 2026.

Secretary Rubio holds a standing invitation to visit Argentina. A Buenos Aires stop was called 'highly probable' for ~12 March 2026 but was shelved amid Middle East escalation; described as a temporary postponement with NO rescheduled date announced as of August 2026.
By early March 2026, FM Quirno had reportedly held seven direct conversations with Rubio that year - the bilateral channel does not depend on summits.

Two major bilateral agreements were already signed in Feb 2026 and are therefore not available to host a signing: the Critical Minerals framework instrument (4 Feb 2026, Quirno + Deputy Secretary Landau at State) and ARTI, the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade and Investment (5 Feb 2026, USTR Greer + Quirno).
Still-pending bilateral instruments that could form a future signing package: a cybersecurity understanding (under development since early 2026) and space/satellite technical agreements.
In July 2026 Argentina unveiled a USD 1.2 billion privately financed ACR-300 SMR (~300 MWe) project by U.S.-based Meitner Energy at the Atucha site - explicitly independent of the 123 Agreement.

The 4th Annual FIRST Latin America & Caribbean regional workshop was co-hosted by the U.S. and Argentina's CNEA in Buenos Aires on 2-4 June 2026 (Ambassador Lamelas and Assistant Secretary Christopher Yeaw attended) - before the window, not in it.
No prediction markets exist on U.S.-Argentina nuclear cooperation across Polymarket, Manifold, or Kalshi.
Argentina has no national election in 2026 (midterms were Oct 2025, next general 2027), so no domestic electoral constraint on signing.

Caveat: the 'text is closed' claim originates from a single source (TN, 10 Aug 2026, unnamed Casa Rosada officials) republished verbatim across many outlets; the official joint statement language is the weaker 'swiftly complete negotiations.'
